Oxylabs and Webshare serve very different customers. Oxylabs is the enterprise heavyweight with a 175M+ residential pool, sales-supported onboarding and scraper APIs. Webshare is the budget, self-service choice of solo developers, with an 80M+ advertised pool, a free datacenter plan and some of the lowest residential prices on the market. blocks.text: Oxylabs in 2026: what you get

Oxylabs sells enterprise-grade proxy infrastructure with a strong reputation among large scraping teams. Its residential network is one of the two largest on the market (175M+ advertised IPs, 195 locations), targeting reaches city, ZIP and ASN level, and its scraper APIs bundle rendering and parsing so you buy results rather than gigabytes. The weak spot for smaller buyers is entry cost: pay-as-you-go runs $8/GB and the cheapest monthly rate needs a $2,500 commitment.

Strengths: One of the two largest residential pools available; Published 99.95% residential success rate; Strong scraper APIs that bill per result; Formal ethical-sourcing documentation for procurement. Weak spots: Expensive at low volume ($8/GB PAYG); Best rates need large monthly commitments; Residential trial goes through sales rather than self-service.
Webshare in 2026: what you get

Webshare is built for developers who want to configure everything themselves. Pricing is transparent, the free datacenter plan makes it easy to test integrations, and paid plans scale smoothly from tiny to large. Its residential network advertises 80M+ IPs across 195 countries. It does not sell mobile proxies or a broad scraping API, and paid plans start with an account-wide limit of 500 concurrent requests.

Strengths: Permanent free datacenter plan for testing; Low, transparent residential pricing; Excellent dashboard and API; Sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Weak spots: Bandwidth resets monthly with no rollover; No mobile proxies; 500-request default concurrency limit.
Pricing: Oxylabs vs Webshare

Oxylabs charges $8/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Monthly plans start with Starter at $30 for 5 GB ($6/GB) and a Basic tier around $100 for 20 GB, and the rate falls to $2.50/GB on the $2,500/month Corporate plan. Mobile traffic starts at $7.50/GB.

Webshare's rotating residential plans cost $3.50 for 1 GB, $27.50 for 10 GB, $65 for 25 GB, $225 for 100 GB and $875 for 500 GB per month, falling to $1.40/GB at 3 TB. Yearly billing is about 30% cheaper but is paid upfront for a 360-day term. Unused bandwidth resets every 30 days.

At 10 GB a month, Webshare is the cheaper option at about $27.50 against $80 for Oxylabs, roughly 66% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Oxylabs does not publish an exact price for that volume; Webshare comes to about $225. Both Oxylabs and Webshare work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Oxylabs has the bigger advertised network, 175M+ residential IPs against 80M+ for Webshare, roughly 2.2 times larger. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Oxylabs lists 195 countries and Webshare lists 195. On targeting, Oxylabs offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while Webshare offers country, plus state, city or ZIP (US) or ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Oxylabs offers rotating and sticky sessions on residential and mobile, and Webshare offers rotating or sticky from 1 minute to 24 hours. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: its pool size and Web Scraper API suit large crawls. How Webshare compares: low prices and a developer-friendly API.
SERP and rank tracking: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its scraper API returns parsed search results. The limitation on the Webshare side: fine for light rank tracking.

Social media and multi-account management: Webshare. Webshare has the edge here. Why: 24-hour sticky sessions and cheap static ISP IPs. How Oxylabs compares: it works, but the pricing is built for volume, not a handful of accounts.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: city and ZIP targeting plus parsed e-commerce endpoints. How Webshare compares: good for US work with ZIP targeting, thinner elsewhere.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: broad geo coverage with ASN targeting. How Webshare compares: no mobile network and limited selector combinations.

Tight budgets: Webshare wins. The deciding factor for Webshare: free tier plus some of the lowest per-GB rates here. The limitation on the Oxylabs side: entry pricing is among the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Oxylabs: Residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer. Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial. Verification and payment rules differ too. Oxylabs: Business verification on larger accounts. Webshare: ID checks only when flagged or for restricted categories. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Oxylabs and Webshare before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Oxylabs and Webshare is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Oxylabs: residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer; Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Oxylabs comes out ahead in 4, Webshare in 2, and 0 are ties. That makes Oxylabs the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Oxylabs is strongest for large scraping pipelines with steady volume, while Webshare is strongest for solo developers and small teams. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
